item/code-induced-balance-entropy-no-go-.title: Code-induced dependence balance and entropy/copy no-go result
item/code-induced-balance-entropy-no-go-.summary:
Accepted statement:

This is an attributed, independently audited port of the consecutive accepted
Yukon artifacts `upper-dependence-balance` and `upper-entropy-nogo`.  They form
one dependency-complete structural result: the first derives a necessary
condition from every deterministic private-message code, and the second proves
that a specified entropy-only relaxation of that condition cannot improve the
classical UV value.

### Finite-block code-induced balance

Let (A) and (B) be independent uniform private messages, encoded
deterministically over (n) uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast
channel.  Receiver (Y) estimates (A) with average error (p_1), and
receiver (Z) estimates (B) with error (p_2).  Define

\[
F_j=h_2(p_j)+p_j\log_2(N_j-1),\qquad \delta_j=F_j/n.
\]

For

\[
S_i=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n),
\]

the exact telescope is

\[
\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[I(A;B\mid S_i,Y_i)-I(A;B\mid S_i,Z_i)\right]
=I(A;B\mid Y^n)-I(A;B\mid Z^n).
\]

Both endpoints are nonnegative, while Fano bounds them by (F_1) and
(F_2), respectively.  With independent uniform time (T), and

\[
U=A,\quad V=B,\quad W=S_T,\quad X=X_T,\quad Y=Y_T,\quad Z=Z_T,
\]

every such code therefore induces

\[
\left|I(U;V\mid W,T,Y)-I(U;V\mid W,T,Z)\right|
\le\max\{\delta_1,\delta_2\}.
\]

The complete induced law retains the fixed coordinate map:

\[
p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=\frac1n p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w\mid u,v,t)
\mathbf 1\{x=f_t(u,v)\}P_{YZ\mid X}(y,z\mid x).
\]

In particular, (U\perp V), (T\perp(U,V)), (X=f_T(U,V)), and the
realized state (W) cannot select another encoder map after (u,v,t) are
fixed.  The same variables satisfy four compatible rate rows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_1&\le I(U,W;Y\mid T)+\delta_1,\\
R_2&\le I(V,W;Z\mid T)+\delta_2,\\
R_1+R_2&\le I(U,W;Y\mid T)+I(X;Z\mid U,W,T)+\delta_1+\delta_2,\\
R_1+R_2&\le I(V,W;Z\mid T)+I(X;Y\mid V,W,T)+\delta_1+\delta_2.
\end{aligned}
\]

This is an exact sequence-level necessary condition.  The alphabets of the
messages and (W) grow with blocklength, so it is not by itself a fixed-
cardinality single-letter outer region.

### Exact entropy/copy no-go theorem

At uniform input, put

\[
h=h_2(1/4),\qquad c=h-1/2,\qquad r=h-3/4.
\]

Consider the coarse entropy relaxation that imposes:

- the complete seven nonempty entropies of the common-noise BSSC coupling,
  namely (H(X)=1), (H(Y)=H(Z)=h),
  (H(X,Y)=H(X,Z)=H(Y,Z)=3/2), and (H(X,Y,Z)=2);
- message/time independence, deterministic encoding, the fixed-map equality,
  the memoryless Markov equality, and exact dependence balance;
- every conditional BEC identity
  (I(L;Y,Z\mid K)=\tfrac12I(L;X\mid K)) for disjoint subtuples
  (L,K\subseteq\{U,V,W,T\}), with (L\ne\varnothing);
- the two sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequalities with right side
  (r).

There is an actual finite entropic point satisfying all these constraints for
which both direct sum branches equal

\[
\boxed{2h_2(1/4)-\frac54
=0.3725562489182657\ldots}.
\]

Consequently, adding any collection of universally valid finite-variable
information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, cannot
lower this relaxation below that value.  Nor can any finite sequence of
standard copy-lemma extensions: each copy step can be realized by conditional
resampling of the finite witness while preserving its original marginal and
objective.

The witness is deliberately not a binary BSSC distribution.  Its (X) is a
tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.  Exact binary-
posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude it and
remain viable.  The theorem obstructs only the stated entropy/copy refinement
route.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The displayed Fano formula is literal for message alphabet sizes N_1,N_2 at least 2; singleton messages require a harmless separate convention.
- The induced auxiliaries have blocklength-dependent alphabets, so the finite-block result is not itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
- The entropy witness is an actual finite distribution but not an actual binary-input BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.
- The no-go result applies only to the specified coarse entropy/universal-inequality/finite-copy relaxation; exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints may exclude the witness.
- The conclusion is an obstruction to that refinement route, not a broadcast-channel capacity bound.

item/uv-product-branchwise-additivity-re.title: UV product and branchwise additivity
item/uv-product-branchwise-additivity-re.summary:
Accepted statement:

This contribution independently ports and rechecks the two accepted Yukon
artifacts `upper-uv-additivity` and `frontier-uv-branchwise`.  They form one
dependency-ordered theorem chain for the two separately relaxed UV sum-rate
rows.

For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel \(W\), write

\[
t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z)
\]

and let \(\mathfrak C\) denote the upper concave envelope on the input
simplex.  Define

\[
A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+\mathfrak C[-t_W](p),
\qquad
D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+\mathfrak C[t_W](p),
\]

\[
B_{\rm avg}(W)=\sup_p\frac{A_W(p)+D_W(p)}2,
\qquad
B_{\rm br}(W)=\sup_p\min\{A_W(p),D_W(p)\}.
\]

The checked claims are:

1. For arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs,
   \[
   B_{\rm avg}(W_1\times W_2)
   =B_{\rm avg}(W_1)+B_{\rm avg}(W_2).
   \]
   The product-channel prior may be correlated and the envelope auxiliary may
   be joint across factors.
2. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges the two receivers, then
   \[
   B_{\rm br}(W)=B_{\rm avg}(W),
   \]
   and the optimum may be restricted to invariant input laws.
3. Finite products preserve this receiver-skew symmetry, so both scalar
   functionals are exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of such
   channels.
4. For the half-skew BSSC \(P\), the unique invariant binary prior is the fair
   prior.  Combining the theorem with the sharp BSSC posterior support already
   represented by canonical transaction
   `c70e1829a7c6a2a8cb8cfc2383f8abf825ac5ea6` gives
   \[
   B_{\rm br}(P^{\times n})=B_{\rm avg}(P^{\times n})
   =n\left(2h_2(1/4)-\frac54\right)
   \]
   for every finite \(n\ge1\).  Numerically, the normalized value is
   \(0.3725562489182657\ldots\) bits per channel use.

The last value is a valid but non-frontier UV converse.  It is weaker than the
current certified full-Theorem-9 capacity upper bound
\(0.369296945969202842443\), so this contribution does not move either endpoint
of the governed capacity interval.

This is an ordinary unregistered contribution.  The UV program lies outside
the registered `yukon-auxiliary-converse-port` scope, and this contribution
does not claim to advance or complete that direction.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The declared reference is required only for the sharp one-letter BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture used in the BSSC specialization; the general product-additivity and symmetry arguments are established internally.
- The resulting UV converse value is non-frontier because it exceeds an already governed stronger benchmark.
- The separate assertion that 0.369296945969202842443 is a certified full-Theorem-9 bound lacks terminal attestation in the packet; this contextual certification claim is not used as a premise and does not affect validity.
- No objective execution attestations were supplied; scripts and hash statements are merely corroborative, while the theorem is supported by the analytic proof.

item/uv-relaxed-converse-tensorization-r.title: Tensorization of separately relaxed UV scalar functionals
item/uv-relaxed-converse-tensorization-r.summary:
Accepted statement:

For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately-relaxed UV sum-rate functional defined in this contribution is exactly additive under products. On a receiver-skew channel the branchwise functional equals the averaged functional, and the same equality and additivity hold for every finite product of receiver-skew channels. Consequently, for the half-skew BSSC P and every integer n >= 1, both functionals on P^{times n} equal n(2 h_2(1/4) - 5/4) bits. This is a theorem only about the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals, not about tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or the capacity itself.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The theorem concerns only the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals.
- It does not establish tensorization of the full UV region, optimization over a common joint (U,V), the GK functional, broadcast-channel capacity, or capacity tensorization.
- The executable attestation checks selected numerical and algebraic facts but not the global support inequality, concave-envelope optimization, or product theorem; those are discharged analytically.
- The README decimal approximation is inaccurate, but the exact expression in the claim is correct and unaffected.

item/finite-grid-q0-foundations-result.title: Finite-grid receiver reduction and exact Q0 foundations
item/finite-grid-q0-foundations-result.summary:
Accepted statement:

Using the accepted private-message 30-row definitions and optimization order of transaction e3c1036ca607539a5ebcddf3058e6014ac5c1cd9, let Q be any N-point posterior grid containing {0,1/2,1}. Every finite-output binary-input receiver has an at-most-N-output replacement with the same mutual-information samples on Q, so inf_{G,K finite} V_Q(G,K) = inf_{|G|,|K|<=N} V_Q(G,K); when Q is reflection closed, inf_{m finite} V_Q(m,m^circ) = inf_{|supp(m)|<=N} V_Q(m,m^circ). For Q0={0,1/2,1} and c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, inf_{G,K finite} V_{Q0}(G,K) = inf_{m finite} V_{Q0}(m,m^circ) = c. Moreover, for every finite-output input-only pair G,K with g=J_G(1/2), k=J_K(1/2), B(G,K) >= V_0(g,k) >= max{F(g),F(k)}, where F(x)=2c max{c,x}/(c+x); consequently, if c <= U < 2c and B(G,K) <= U, then 2c^2/U-c <= g,k <= Uc/(2c-U). These are finite-grid and necessary-coercivity statements only, with no continuum cardinality, limit interchange, or full-functional reflected-optimality assertion.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The result is limited to finite posterior grids and finite-output receivers.
- The reflected-class conclusion is proved only for reflection-closed finite grids; no full-functional reflected-optimality assertion is established.
- No continuum cardinality theorem, attainment claim, limit interchange, capacity-converse interpretation, or improved sum-capacity bound is established.
- The declared reference is needed for the accepted 30-row definitions, optimization order, single-output term structure, and the inequality V_Q(G,K) <= B(G,K); external manuscript authenticity is not required.

item/two-letter-marton-two-symbol-prunin.title: Two-letter Marton two-symbol support pruning
item/two-letter-marton-two-symbol-prunin.summary:
Accepted statement:

Assume the Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang theorem that Marton's private-message sum-rate for every binary-input broadcast channel equals randomized time division. For the half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input X_1X_2 is supported on at most two of {00,01,10,11} has sum-rate strictly below 0.615 bits. Consequently, because the product randomized-time-division value is greater than 0.7232857688439092 bits, every strict two-letter Marton improvement over the current BSSC achievable rate must use at least three super-input symbols. This is only a support-pruning result and does not rule out a gain on three- or four-symbol support.

- The result only excludes supports of cardinality at most two and makes no assertion against gains using three- or four-symbol support.

item/conditional-product-marton-no-gain-.title: Conditional-product Marton no-gain theorem and correlation ledger
item/conditional-product-marton-no-gain-.summary:
Accepted statement:

Let T be any finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channel, and let M_T be its one-letter private-message Marton sum-rate. For every n >= 1, the supremum of the n-letter Marton functional over laws P(w,u^n,v^n,x^n)=P(w) product_i P_i(u_i,v_i,x_i|w), with aggregate U=(U_i) and V=(V_i), equals n M_T. The common W is arbitrary and may correlate coordinates unconditionally. Consequently, any strict two-letter gain for the half-skew BSSC must use a law outside this conditional-product class: every chosen coordinate-packet decomposition under which the factorization could be tested must fail it. For the broader class of arbitrary finite tuple laws P(w,u^n,v^n,x^n), with a chosen aggregate U=(U_i), V=(V_i) and the product channel, the exact total-correlation residual identity in README equation (11) holds, so any strict gain must satisfy the correlation-balance inequality (13) for that decomposition. Trivial constant padding always supplies a tuple representation, but the ledger and its pruning usefulness depend on the noncanonical decomposition. These results do not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact BSSC capacity.

The equations expressly incorporated by that accepted statement are, for the chosen tuple decomposition,

\[
\begin{aligned}
&L_{1/2,T^{\otimes n}}(P)-\sum_iL_{1/2,T}(P^{(i)})\\
&\quad=\operatorname{TC}(U^n\mid W)+G_{UY}+G_{VZ}-G_{UV}\\
&\qquad\quad-\tfrac12\big[\operatorname{TC}(Y^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Y^n)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n)\big],
\end{aligned}
\]

and any strict gain forces

\[
\operatorname{TC}(U^n\mid W)+G_{UY}+G_{VZ}-G_{UV}
>\tfrac12\big[\operatorname{TC}(Y^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Y^n)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n\mid W)+\operatorname{TC}(Z^n)\big].
\]

Here \(\operatorname{TC}(A^n\mid C)=\sum_iH(A_i\mid C)-H(A^n\mid C)\), \(\operatorname{TC}(A^n)=\sum_iH(A_i)-H(A^n)\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{UY}&=\sum_iH(Y_i\mid U_i,W)-H(Y^n\mid U^n,W),\\
G_{VZ}&=\sum_iH(Z_i\mid V_i,W)-H(Z^n\mid V^n,W),\\
G_{UV}&=\sum_iH(U_i\mid V_i,W)-H(U^n\mid V^n,W).
\end{aligned}
\]

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The theorem applies to finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channels and to the specified conditional-product factorization with a common W that may induce unconditional coordinate correlation.
- A strict-gain law must fail the conditional-product factorization for every exact chosen coordinate-packet decomposition to which the theorem applies.
- For arbitrary tuple laws, the residual ledger and correlation-balance condition are relative to the chosen aggregate coordinate decomposition; they are noncanonical.
- Inequality (13) is only a necessary condition for strict gain, not a sufficient condition.
- Constant padding supplies a tuple representation, but does not make the ledger canonical or necessarily useful for pruning.
- The result does not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact half-skew BSSC capacity.

item/conditional-product-marton-no-gain-.title: Receiver-skew symmetrization and entropy-ledger proof
item/conditional-product-marton-no-gain-.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. Receiver-skew reflection followed by fair-selector symmetrization identifies the one-letter Marton supremum with its midpoint affine functional without assuming attainment. Under the stated conditional-product factorization, the satellite mutual-information terms add exactly coordinatewise, while the common-output terms are subadditive; applying the one-letter bound to each coordinate gives the upper bound n M_T. Independent epsilon-optimal one-letter copies give the reverse inequality. For arbitrary tuple laws over the product channel, direct entropy expansion yields the accepted total-correlation residual identity and makes the stated correlation-balance inequality necessary for any strict gain. This proof item is limited to the linked accepted claim and does not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or exact BSSC capacity.

item/two-letter-padding-correlation-test.title: Four padding-correlation tests for a two-letter Marton gain
item/two-letter-padding-correlation-test.summary:
Accepted statement:

Assume canonical transaction 5ed3f525b9ae7f32c6e1dcbf22ecdb5ae946a4a6 and its exact tuple-law total-correlation residual. For any finite receiver-skew broadcast channel T and any arbitrary finite two-letter Marton law P(W,U,V,X_1,X_2), define A_1=I(Y_2;Y_1,U|W), A_2=I(Y_1;Y_2,U|W), B_1=I(Z_2;Z_1,V|W), B_2=I(Z_1;Z_2,V|W), D=I(U;V|W), and C=(I(Y_1;Y_2|W)+I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2|W)+I(Z_1;Z_2))/2. If this law has Marton value strictly above 2M_T, then A_a+B_b>C+1{a!=b}D for all four (a,b) in {1,2}^2. Hence failure of any one inequality rules out a gain. Adding the crossed tests gives the combined necessary inequality in README equation (12). Applied to the half-skew BSSC, these tests cover every abstract two-letter auxiliary law without assuming an a priori tuple structure. They are necessary only and do not prove additivity, exhibit a gain, or determine capacity.

The combined necessary inequality expressly referenced as README equation (12) is

\[
\begin{aligned}
&I(Y_1;Y_2\mid W)+I(Z_1;Z_2\mid W)
-I(Y_1;Y_2)-I(Z_1;Z_2)\\
&\quad+I(U;Y_2\mid Y_1,W)+I(U;Y_1\mid Y_2,W)\\
&\quad+I(V;Z_2\mid Z_1,W)+I(V;Z_1\mid Z_2,W)
>2I(U;V\mid W).
\end{aligned}
\]

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The inequalities are necessary only; they do not prove additivity, exhibit a gaining law, establish sufficiency, or determine capacity.
- The summed crossed condition is weaker than retaining the two crossed inequalities separately.
- The result concerns finite receiver-skew broadcast channels and finite auxiliary alphabets.
- Numerical checker attestations are corroborative only; the universal conclusion rests on the analytic entropy identities.

item/two-letter-padding-correlation-test.title: Four constant-padding residual proof

item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.title: Finite-auxiliary Marton multiletter foundation and directed RTD threshold
item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed half-skew BSSC P and every n >= 1, define M_n^fin(P) as the supremum of the displayed private-message Marton functional over finite auxiliary alphabets U,V,W and finite laws (U,V,W)-X^n-(Y^n,Z^n). Unconditionally, 0 <= M_n^fin(P) <= 2n, M_{m+n}^fin(P) >= M_m^fin(P)+M_n^fin(P), and Fekete's lemma gives lim_n M_n^fin(P)/n = sup_n M_n^fin(P)/n; k independent copies of a selected n-letter law of value S_n have value exactly k S_n. Assume (H-Marton), the exact finite-DMBC private-message Marton achievability theorem stated in the README. Then C_sum(P) >= M_n^fin(P)/n for every n and hence C_sum(P) is at least the displayed Fekete limit. For the exact BSSC randomized-time-division value L_RTD, the README's symmetrization and calculus proof gives the stated closed form at q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30, and the directed standard-library certificate proves the strict intervals 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028007 < L_RTD < 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028008 and 0.7232857688439092313268831563011740144159620214477211104074274596056014 < 2 L_RTD < 0.7232857688439092313268831563011740144159620214477211104074274596056016. Assume additionally (H-binary), the exact binary-input Marton-equals-randomized-time-division theorem stated in the README; then M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD. Under (H-Marton), a selected finite n-letter law strictly improves the governed RTD achievable lower bound through super-symbol normalization iff S_n > n L_RTD; under both hypotheses this is equivalently a strict improvement over the complete one-letter Marton sum optimum. This append-only claim repairs only the finite-auxiliary scope, conditional super-symbol conclusion, conditional one-letter identification, and decimal certification of transaction f6ea30479b9ca461294ba89a8a1a31c06ce59d08; that transaction is a corrective/provenance reference rather than a mathematical premise. No fixed-n equality is a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The capacity lower bound C_sum(P) >= M_n^fin(P)/n and the resulting Fekete-limit lower bound are conditional on (H-Marton).
- The identity M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD is conditional on (H-binary).
- Equivalence between improvement over RTD and improvement over the complete one-letter Marton optimum requires both (H-Marton) and (H-binary).
- All optimizations defining M_n^fin(P) are restricted to finite auxiliary alphabets; no optimizer or cardinality theorem is assumed.
- No fixed-n equality is asserted or used as a capacity converse.
- The declared transaction is corrective/provenance material only and is not a mathematical dependency.

item/two-letter-marton-full-support-nece.title: Full-support and mass-floor necessity for a two-letter Marton gain
item/two-letter-marton-full-support-nece.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input X_1X_2 is supported on at most three of {00,01,10,11} has unnormalized Marton sum value strictly below 0.695 bits. A fair one-letter randomized-time-division schedule with reflected rational conditional priors 1/6 and 5/6, repeated independently twice, has exact unnormalized value B_{1/6}=2h_2(1/4)+h_2(1/12)-h_2(5/12)-1/3>0.7231 bits. Therefore every strict two-letter Marton improvement over twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value must assign positive mass to all four super-input symbols. Quantitatively, every such improving witness must assign mass greater than 1/180 to each of 00 and 11 and mass greater than 1/325 to each of 01 and 10. This is a support-pruning theorem for the two-letter Marton functional, not a full-support no-gain theorem or an unrestricted capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The result concerns the unnormalized two-letter Marton functional for the half-skew BSSC product channel.
- It is a support-pruning theorem only; it does not prove that full-support Marton laws cannot yield a gain.
- It is not a converse for unrestricted broadcast coding or a determination of unrestricted sum capacity.
- The numerical attestation supports the finite algebraic and numerical inequalities, while the universal Marton reduction and calculus steps are established in the written proof.

item/two-letter-marton-full-support-nece.title: Support-line, face-orbit, and mass-floor proof
item/two-letter-marton-full-support-nece.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It derives one-letter BSSC support lines by calculus, lifts them through an exact two-factor chain-rule identity, and obtains two direct UV-style bounds reducing every two-letter Marton value to G(P_S)+2r. Channel symmetries split the four three-symbol faces into two orbits; concavity and explicit one-variable maximization or a rational tangent bound give the strict 0.695-bit ceiling. A finite independently repeated rational randomized-time-division law supplies the accepted comparison value. Finally, indicator decomposition relative to each omitted symbol and monotonicity of the resulting entropy bound yield the four strict mass floors. The proof is limited to the accepted support-pruning claim and does not rule out a gain from full-support laws.

item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.title: Marginal-balance and correlation necessities for a two-letter Marton gain
item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, let M be the unnormalized finite-auxiliary Marton sum value of any law (W,U,V)-X_1X_2-(Y^2,Z^2), let q_i=Pr[X_i=1], Q=q_1+q_2, let C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2), and let c_in=P(X_1X_2=11)-q_1q_2. Canonical transaction 33a5944dca980bf94cc869c6c7dee2d04385ff58 supplies the two pre-averaging Marton-to-input rows and their universal average M <= G(P_{X_1X_2})+2r, while canonical transaction 88a1004f309460f3ec1cacdae88d30f88559f9bc supplies the exact directed threshold T=2L_RTD. The exact identity G=F(q_1)+F(q_2)-C_out/2 and the coordinatewise concave row envelopes imply that M>T forces q_1,q_2 in (3/8,5/8), hence in (7/20,13/20), together with 17/20<Q<23/20, C_out<7/160=0.04375<0.044 bits, and |c_in|<7/40. On the reflected/transposed family P(00)=P(11)=alpha and P(01)=P(10)=1/2-alpha, a gain additionally forces 1/8<alpha<5/13. These are necessary conditions only; they do not establish a two-letter gain, rule one out, or give a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- Applies to the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}.
- Applies to the unnormalized finite-auxiliary Marton sum value.
- The conclusions are necessary conditions conditional on M>T.
- It neither constructs nor proves a two-letter gain.
- It does not rule out a two-letter gain.
- It is not a capacity converse.
- From the threshold reference, only the unconditional RTD calculus and interval certificate are needed; neither (H-Marton) nor (H-binary) is used.

item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.title: Output-correlation decomposition and concave-envelope pruning proof
item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim.
